questions.question: The quadratic equation [latex]x^{2}-4x+4=0[/latex] is to be solved numerically, starting with the initial guess [latex]x_0=3[/latex]. The Newton-Raphson method is applied once to get a new estimate and then the Secant method is applied once using the initial guess and this new estimate. The estimated value of the root after the application of the Secant method is __________.
questions.explanation: [latex] \begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=x^{2}-4x+4 \\   {f}'\left ( x \right )&=2x-4 \\   x_{0}&=3 \\   f\left ( 3 \right )&=1, {f}'\left ( 3 \right )=2 \\ \text{By Newton } & \text{Rapshon method,}\\   x_{1}&=x_{0}-\frac{f\left ( x_{0} \right )}{{f}'_{x_{0}}} \\    &=3-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\   f\left ( \frac{5}{2} \right )&=\frac{25}{4}-10+4=\frac{1}{4} \\ & \text{By Secant method,}\\   x_{2}&=x_{1}-\frac{\left ( x_{1}-x_{0} \right )f\left ( x_{1} \right )}{f\left ( x_{1} \right )-f\left ( x_{0} \right )} \\    &=\frac{f_{1}x_{0}-f_{0}x_{1}}{f_{1}-f_{0}} \\    &=\frac{\left ( \frac{1}{4}\times 3 \right )-\left ( 1\times \frac{5}{2} \right )}{\frac{1}{4}-1} \\    &=\frac{7}{3}=2.33 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex] \begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=x^{2}-4x+4 \\   {f}'\left ( x \right )&=2x-4 \\   x_{0}&=3 \\   f\left ( 3 \right )&=1, {f}'\left ( 3 \right )=2 \\ \text{By Newton } & \text{Rapshon method,}\\   x_{1}&=x_{0}-\frac{f\left ( x_{0} \right )}{{f}'_{x_{0}}} \\    &=3-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\   f\left ( \frac{5}{2} \right )&=\frac{25}{4}-10+4=\frac{1}{4} \\ & \text{By Secant method,}\\   x_{2}&=x_{1}-\frac{\left ( x_{1}-x_{0} \right )f\left ( x_{1} \right )}{f\left ( x_{1} \right )-f\left ( x_{0} \right )} \\    &=\frac{f_{1}x_{0}-f_{0}x_{1}}{f_{1}-f_{0}} \\    &=\frac{\left ( \frac{1}{4}\times 3 \right )-\left ( 1\times \frac{5}{2} \right )}{\frac{1}{4}-1} \\    &=\frac{7}{3}=2.33 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider the following complex function: [latex]f(z)=\frac{9}{(z-1)(z+2)^{2}}[/latex] Which of the following is one of the residues of the above function?
questions.explanation: [latex]f(z)[/latex] has poles at [latex]z=1, -2[/latex] Residue of [latex]f(z)[/latex] at [/latex](z=1)[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned}  &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 1}\left ( z-1 \right )f\left ( z \right ) \\   &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 1}\frac{9}{\left ( z+2 \right )^{2}} \\&=1 \end{aligned}[/latex] Residue of [latex]f(z)[/latex] at [latex](z=-2)[/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned}  &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\frac{d}{dz^{2-1}}\left [ \left ( z+2 \right )^{2}f\left ( z \right ) \right ] \\   &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\frac{d}{dz}\left ( \frac{9}{z-1} \right ) \\   &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\left ( \frac{9}{\left ( z-1 \right )^{2}} \right ) \\   &=-1\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In Newton-Raphson iterative method, the initial guess value ( [latex]x_{ini}[/latex]) is considered as zero while finding the roots of the euation:[latex]f(x)=-2+6x-4x^{2}+0.5x^{3}[/latex]. The correction, [latex]\Delta x[/latex], to be added to [latex]x_{ini}[/latex] in the first iteration is____________.
questions.explanation: [latex] \begin{aligned}   f\left ( x \right )&=-2+6x-4x^{2}+0.5x^{3} \\    {f}'\left ( x \right )&=6-8x+1.5x^{2} \\    x_{ini}&=0\\ \text{By Newton }&\text{Raphson Method,}\\    x_{1}&=x_{ini}-\frac{f\left ( x_{ini} \right )}{{f}'\left ( x_{ini} \right )} \\    &=  0-\frac{-2}{6} \\ \Rightarrow    \;\;x_{1}&=\frac{1}{3} \\ \therefore \;\;  \Delta x&=x_{1}-x_{ini}=\frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

&=\frac{1}{2}\left[y^{2}-x^{2}-y^{2}+x^{2}\right] \\
&=0
\end{aligned}[/latex] Hence, flow is irrotational.
